surviving_claim: The file is not retracted and 9 of its 12 records are untouched by the defect. Every record verifies cleanly against the panel it was run under: verify_use_records returns no problem for this file against a panel materialised from the git blobs at bdf12d5 and 84d2094 (manifest 15e588a86c12, verify_freeze []). What does not survive is the reading of 3 records as current results for the regenerated panel. Those 3 claim a quality verdict on a within-graph cell that A20 rewrote, and against the new panel they recompute to a different verdict. Affected cells: ad01-w2-within-gr-00, ad01-w2-within-gr-01, ad01-w2-within-gr-02. Re-stamping the digest would convert a withdrawn measurement into a current one, which is why this is a scope and not an edit.
note: artifact_sha256 is the git blob digest, so the marker is bound to the committed bytes rather than to one host line-ending policy. On a core.autocrlf checkout sha256_file sees CRLF and reports this marker stale; that is the checkout, not the artifact, and it is fixed by scoping the evidence trees in .gitattributes. Re-stamping freeze_digest to ee1362df3f09 is not a repair: it makes the checker pass by asserting that a quality verdict obtained against a regenerated cell is current.
